I am a 40-year-old woman farming about 8 mu of land here in Quzhou County. My family has been on this plot for generations, and I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent tells me, but at the end of the day I trust what I see with my own eyes and what the neighbors are doing.

This year I will stick with the wheat-maize double cropping system on all 8 mu. I thought about trying cotton like some folks in the southern part of the county, but cotton takes too much hand-picking labor and the price fluctuates too much. With wheat and maize, even if one crop has a bad year, the other usually carries us through, and the grain station is reliable. The wheat is already in the ground from last October — I planted an improved variety, liangxing-series, same as my neighbor Lao Zhang used last year and he got over 1000 jin per mu. For the summer maize, I will plant a hybrid variety like Nongda 372; everyone uses hybrid seed for maize now because the yield is just too good to pass up, even though the seed costs more than saving your own.

For fertilizer, the extension guy recommended about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu for wheat, but I know from experience that is not quite enough for our soil. I usually put down a compound fertilizer base of about 100 jin per mu — that gives me roughly 18-20 kg of N, 22 kg of P₂O₅, and 7-8 kg of K₂O per mu. Then at wheat jointing in spring I topdress with another 15 kg of urea per mu. For maize, I apply compound fertilizer at planting for about 22 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O per mu. I would rather apply a little too much than too little — a bad year hurts more than wasting a few yuan on extra fertilizer.

Irrigation is expensive because we pump groundwater, but you cannot skip it. I will irrigate the wheat three times: one winter irrigation, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. For maize, two times is enough — one right after planting if it is dry, and one at the big flare stage. 

Tillage is straightforward: I rotary-tilled before planting wheat last autumn, and for maize there is no time to till after wheat harvest — we have to plant within a few days, so everyone does no-tillage for maize. I hire a machine for sowing.

For pesticides, I will spray herbicide once on each crop and insecticide twice — wheat gets aphids and maize gets armyworms if you are not careful. That is about 3 applications per crop.

I expect about 1000 kg per mu for wheat and 1100 kg per mu for maize if the weather cooperates. Last year was decent and I got close to that, so I am hopeful.
